summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Reported to House):

blocks.text: This bill allows the National Park Service (NPS) to expedite the approval of contracts to restore forests, structures, and assets within areas of the Grand Canyon National Park impacted by the Dragon Bravo Fire in Arizona.

Specifically, the bill authorizes the NPS to use emergency acquisition flexibilities without a presidential emergency or disaster declaration to contract for the following services in such impacted areas: managing or restoring forests, rebuilding structures affected by the fire, improving grounds and structures, conducting recovery efforts, or other specified activities.

This authority expires on the date that is the earlier of the following: (1) seven years after the date of this bill's enactment, or (2) the date on which projects and recovery efforts within such area are completed. The NPS may request Congress extend such authority for 12 months if a new wildfire ignites within such area and impacts recovery efforts related to the Dragon Bravo Fire.

The bill also authorizes the NPS to enter into noncompetitive procurement contracts for rebuilding, rehabilitating, replacing, or operating assets, such as lodging or utilities, to support the recovery and reopening of the Grand Canyon National Park North Rim. This authority is conditioned upon the NPS making certain determinations regarding the North Rim concessioner and it terminates seven years after this bill's enactment.

This bill lets the National Park Service speed up contracts to restore forests, buildings, and other assets in the parts of Grand Canyon National Park that were damaged by the Dragon Bravo Fire in Arizona. The agency can use its emergency contracting powers in those areas without needing a presidential emergency or disaster declaration. The work covered includes managing or restoring forests, rebuilding structures damaged by the fire, improving grounds and buildings, carrying out recovery efforts, and other listed activities.

This emergency contracting authority ends on whichever comes first: seven years after the bill is enacted, or the day the projects and recovery work in those areas are finished. If a new wildfire starts in the same area and affects the Dragon Bravo recovery, the agency may ask Congress to extend the authority by 12 months.

The bill also lets the Park Service sign noncompetitive contracts, meaning contracts awarded without an open competition, to rebuild, repair, replace, or run assets such as lodging and utilities. These are meant to help recover and reopen the North Rim of the park. This option depends on the Park Service making certain determinations about the North Rim concessioner, the company that runs visitor services there, and it also expires seven years after the bill is enacted.
